content.user_title: Build React Native Apps with Expo
content.value_statement: Mobile development requires different tools, layouts, and behavior for iOS and Android. This skill provides React Native and Expo patterns for setup, components, platform choices, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Lists standard commands for starting React Native and Expo development workflows.
Provides a typed React Native component structure with styles and press handling.
Shows conditional rendering and style selection for iOS and Android.
Demonstrates FlatList, TextInput, and loading-state component patterns.
Recommends accessibility, responsive design, navigation, and state-management practices.
Lists troubleshooting steps for Metro, native modules, builds, and simulators.
limitations: It does not create a complete application architecture or project files.
It does not replace testing on physical devices and supported simulators.
It does not cover every native module, deployment workflow, or store requirement.
Commands may require local Node.js, Expo, Android, or iOS tooling.

use_cases.title: Start a mobile prototype
use_cases.description: Use the setup and component guidance to begin an Expo or React Native prototype.

use_cases.title: Adapt an interface by platform
use_cases.description: Apply the platform selection examples when iOS and Android need different UI behavior or styles.

use_cases.title: Resolve local development issues
use_cases.description: Use the troubleshooting guidance when Metro, native modules, builds, or simulators fail.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple React Native screen with a title, a button, and accessible labels. Explain how to run it with Expo.

prompt_templates.title: Build a responsive list
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build a React Native FlatList for product data. Include stable keys, loading state, and responsive item styling.

prompt_templates.title: Add platform-specific behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to make this React Native component use iOS and Android specific spacing and shadows while keeping shared code.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an Expo build
prompt_templates.prompt: My Expo build fails after adding a native module. Give a safe diagnostic plan for app configuration, prebuild, and simulator testing.

output_examples.input: Create an accessible React Native action button.
output: A component structure with a press handler and reusable styles.
Accessibility labels and roles for screen-reader support.
Instructions for testing the button on a simulator or device.

output_examples.input: Make a card look appropriate on iOS and Android.
output: Platform-selected shadow styling for iOS and elevation for Android.
A short explanation of which values differ by platform.

output_examples.input: Metro will not start in my Expo project.
output: The Expo cache-clearing command to run after reviewing local project state.
Follow-up checks for configuration and simulator issues.

best_practices: Test layouts and interactions on both iOS and Android before release.
Add accessibility labels and roles when creating interactive components.
Use reusable styles and optimized images to reduce rendering cost.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on one platform when validating mobile behavior.
Do not use unstable list keys or render large lists without FlatList.
Do not run cleanup or prebuild commands without understanding their local project effects.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers React Native and Expo setup, components, platform differences, common patterns, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does it support both iOS and Android?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for conditional rendering and platform-specific style values.

faq.question: Does it create native project files?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples rather than a complete generated project.

faq.question: Can it help with Expo commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents common Expo start, install, prebuild, and troubleshooting commands.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends accessibility labels and roles for interactive components.

faq.question: Should I run the listed commands without review?
faq.answer: No. Review each command for its effect on your local project and environment before running it.
